panels.rationale: The peripheral blood smear shows blast cells, one of which is indicated as a megakaryoblast (arrow). Megakaryoblasts are abnormal myeloid blasts and are characteristic of transient abnormal myelopoiesis (TAM), as supported by the figure's context and caption.
panels.attribution_text: Mishra et al. Transient Abnormal Myelopoiesis: An Abnormal Course and the Efficacy of Delayed Treatment.. Cureus 2024. doi:10.7759/cureus.54219. CC BY (https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/). Figure 1.
in_text_mentions: Routine investigations revealed anemia (hematocrit: 23%), thrombocytopenia (19000/mm3), leucocytosis (86200/mm3), and coagulopathy (International Normalized Ratio 3). Peripheral smear showed 75% blasts with megakaryoblastic origin with flow cytometry positivity for CD 34, CD 7, CD 71, CD 41, CD 56, CD 33, CD 58, CD 117 and negativity for MPO, CD3, CD19, CD 64, CD14, CD 13, CD 66c, CD 10, CD 20, CD 79a, human leukocyte antigen - DR isotype (HLA-DR) suggestive of TAM (Figure 1, Figure 2). Chest X-ray showed right lower lobe consolidation.

panels.rationale: Whole-figure plate of 2 panels (A, B). A: Panel A displays the low-power histopathology of the placenta (H&E) showing the context of vascular involvement, consistent with widespread fetal hematologic involvement of transient abnormal myelopoiesis. B: Panel B provides high-magnification histopathological evidence of the key finding: intravascular blasts (mononuclear cells with a high nuclear-to-cytoplasmic ratio) within the vessel lumina of the placenta, confirming the involvement of transient abnormal myelopoiesis.
panels.attribution_text: Tanaka et al. Unexpected Cardiotocographic Deterioration in Fetal Transient Abnormal Myelopoiesis.. Cureus 2026. doi:10.7759/cureus.116943. CC BY (https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/). Figure 2.
panels.figure_caption: Histopathological findings of the placenta (hematoxylin–eosin staining). (A) Low-power view showing fetal vessels within the chorionic villi and both arteries and veins at the placental insertion site of the umbilical cord. The boxed area corresponds to the higher-magnification image shown in panel B (×20). (B) High-power view demonstrating numerous intravascular mononuclear cells with a high nuclear-to-cytoplasmic ratio consistent with blasts (arrowheads) within the vessel lumina (×40).
in_text_mentions: ental examination showed a weight of 446 g (approximately the 10th percentile for gestational age). The umbilical cord measured 19 cm in length and contained three vessels. Histopathological examination of the placenta revealed numerous mononuclear cells with a high nuclear-to-cytoplasmic ratio, consistent with blasts, within the vascular lumina of the chorionic villi and within both arteries and veins at the placental insertion site of the umbilical cord (Figure 2). This distribution indicated widespread intravascular fetal hematologic involvement rather than localized placental infiltration.
